findings.title: Human messenger as embodied bearer, not sign-producer
findings.claim: The close holds human embodiment and message-bearing together: the envoy's bodily humanity need not disqualify him from carrying revelation, while sign-giving remains God's prerogative. A recipient-fit implication is possible because wider examples depict human messengers as embodied, but it is not stated as a universal rule.
findings.mechanism: The focus pairs basharan with rasulan. The wider pattern of human recipients of revelation who eat, the definition of message delivery as the messenger's task, and the restriction of signs to divine permission return through bashar, rasul, and rabbi; together they distinguish embodied transmission from producing the demanded spectacle.
findings.reader_payoff: The final answer reads as a placement of office and jurisdiction, not simply a confession of inability: a human bearer delivers the message, while the Lord controls signs.
findings.containment: This is a qualified cross-text synthesis, not proof that 17:93 states a general audience-fit law or that the messenger has no other capacity. The global links establish embodiment, delivery, and sign limits more clearly than a universal recipient-fit principle, and they do not establish the challengers' motive.

epistemic.reason: The focus-anchored publication is trusted; the represented HFT formulation is legacy_unbound, and the recipient-fit implication remains an inference from exact wider texts.

findings.title: A demanded condition does not guarantee belief
findings.claim: The focus makes belief conditional on a further readable-book demand. Wider passages show that even a promised sign or imagined extreme evidences do not guarantee belief, so the condition is not itself proof that its fulfillment would produce acceptance.
findings.mechanism: The focus's belief carrier returns through 6:109, where a sworn promise after a sign is questioned, and 6:111, where angels and the dead speaking still do not compel belief apart from God's will.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's until-condition can be read as a stated threshold without treating the threshold as a reliable cause of belief.
findings.containment: This does not establish that the focus is the climax of the local 17:90-92 sequence, that belief is indefinitely deferred, or that the requesters are consciously insincere.

epistemic.reason: The HFT nomination is unanchored, but the exact focus belief form and supplied 6:109 and 6:111 texts support the narrower cross-text comparison.

findings.title: The readable book also echoes personal accountability
findings.claim: Elsewhere earlier in the same surah, each person is given an open book and told to read their own book. This returns through the focus's book-and-reading pair and makes the requested document resonate with a personal record, not only an external proof object.
findings.mechanism: The exact book language in 17:13-14 and the imperative to read one's book contact kitaban naqra'uhu in the focus, shifting the wider resonance from a text requested of the messenger to a record encountered by its subject.
findings.reader_payoff: The same book-reading image can face in two directions: an audience asks to inspect a text, while elsewhere the reader faces their own account.
findings.containment: The focus's demanded book is not identified with the eschatological record. The connection note's description of 17:14 as later is chronologically inconsistent with its verse number; it is used only as a preceding same-surah echo.

epistemic.reason: Exact supplied Arabic shares the book and reading images, while the different functions of the passages keep the interpretation analogical and bounded.

findings.title: A later audience answers recitation with tasbih
findings.claim: In the later same-surah recitation scene, knowledgeable listeners respond with subhana rabbina and prostrate in humility. That phrase echoes the focus's commanded subhana rabbi and places the messenger's reply beside a later receptive response to recitation.
findings.mechanism: The focus's tasbih carrier returns in 17:108's exact phrase, while 17:107 and 17:109 frame it with recitation and a humble audience response.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's God-directed reply resonates not only as a response to demanded signs but as part of a wider contrast between demanding more proof and receiving recitation with humility.
findings.containment: The later audience and the focus speaker are not equated, and the surrounding verses do not prove that the demanded book and the recited Qur'an are identical.

epistemic.reason: The exact repeated tasbih phrase and supplied adjacent recitation scene support a clear echo, while the difference of speakers and scenes limits the inference.
